entries.25:44: They are surprised and ask when they ever saw Jesus in need and failed to help. It shows that people can miss the needs right in front of them and not even realize it.
entries.25:45: Jesus answers that whatever was not done for the least important person was not done for him. It means that how we treat the overlooked and needy is how we treat Jesus himself.
entries.25:46: The outcome is set: one group faces lasting punishment and the other lasting life. It means our choices about caring for others matter for where we end up.
entries.26:1: Jesus finished all his teaching and then spoke to his disciples. It shows his public teaching was done and something serious was coming next.
entries.26:2: Jesus told his disciples that in two days it would be Passover, and he would be handed over to be killed on a cross. He was warning them plainly about his death.
entries.26:3: The top priests and the leaders of the people met together at the house of Caiaphas, the high priest. The religious leaders were gathering to plot against Jesus.
entries.26:4: They planned together to arrest Jesus by some trick and kill him. These leaders were determined to get rid of him secretly.
entries.26:5: They agreed not to do it during the festival, because they were afraid the people would riot. They wanted to avoid public outrage.
entries.26:6: Jesus was in Bethany, staying at the house of Simon, a man who had leprosy. He was spending time with people others might avoid.
entries.26:7: A woman came with an expensive bottle of perfume and poured it on Jesus' head while he sat at the table. She was honoring him in a costly way.
entries.26:8: The disciples were upset and asked why the perfume was wasted. They thought it was a foolish use of something valuable.
entries.26:9: They said the perfume could have been sold for a lot of money and given to the poor. They were thinking about the money it cost.
entries.26:10: Jesus saw their anger and told them to stop bothering the woman, because she had done something kind for him. He defended her when others criticized her.
entries.26:11: Jesus said the poor would always be around, but he would not always be with them. He was pointing out that this was a special moment to honor him.
entries.26:12: By pouring the perfume on his body, she was preparing him for his burial. She did it without knowing it, but it pointed to his coming death.
entries.26:13: Jesus said that wherever the good news is told in the whole world, this woman's act would be remembered too. Her kindness would be told alongside the gospel.
entries.26:14: One of the twelve disciples, Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests. He was turning against Jesus and going to the people who wanted to kill him.
entries.26:15: Judas asked what they would pay him to hand Jesus over, and they agreed on thirty pieces of silver. He betrayed Jesus for a set amount of money.
entries.26:16: From then on, Judas looked for a good chance to hand Jesus over to them. He was actively waiting for the right moment to betray him.
entries.26:17: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples asked Jesus where they should prepare the Passover meal. They wanted to know where to set things up.
entries.26:18: Jesus told them to go into the city to a certain man and tell him the Teacher said his time was near and he would eat the Passover at his house with his disciples. He arranged the meal ahead of time.
entries.26:19: The disciples did what Jesus told them and got the Passover meal ready. They obeyed his instructions exactly.
entries.26:20: When evening came, Jesus sat down at the table with the twelve disciples. They were gathered for the Passover meal together.
entries.26:21: While they were eating, Jesus said plainly that one of them would betray him. He told them the painful truth ahead of time.
entries.26:22: The disciples were very sad and asked him one by one, "Is it I, Lord?" They were worried and wanted to know it wasn't them.
entries.26:23: Jesus answered that the one who dips his hand in the dish with him is the one who will betray him. He pointed out that the betrayer was someone close to him at the table.
entries.26:24: Jesus said he would die as the Scriptures said, but terrible trouble awaits the man who betrays him; it would have been better for that man never to have been born. Betraying Jesus is a serious and tragic thing.
entries.26:25: Judas, the one betraying him, asked, "Is it I, Master?" and Jesus said yes. Jesus did not hide the truth from Judas.
entries.26:26: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, "Take it; this is my body." He was giving them a picture of his body being given for them.
entries.26:27: Jesus took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them to drink. He shared the cup with his disciples as part of the meal.
entries.26:28: Jesus said the cup was his blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. His death would bring forgiveness to people.
entries.26:29: Jesus said he would not drink wine again until he drinks it new with them in his Father's kingdom. He was looking ahead to a future celebration with them.
entries.26:30: After singing a song of praise to God, they went out to the Mount of Olives. They left the meal and went to a place they knew well.
entries.26:31: Jesus told them that all of them would run away from him that night, because the Scriptures say the shepherd would be struck and the sheep scattered. He warned them that their courage would fail.
entries.26:32: Jesus said that after he rose from the dead, he would go ahead of them to Galilee. He was already pointing them toward what would happen after his death.
entries.26:33: Peter told Jesus that even if everyone else turned away, he never would. He was confident he would stay loyal.
entries.26:34: Jesus told Peter that before the rooster crowed that very night, Peter would deny him three times. He warned Peter that his confidence would break.
entries.26:35: Peter said that even if he had to die with Jesus, he would never deny him, and all the other disciples said the same. They all promised to stay faithful, though they didn't know what was coming.
entries.26:36: Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane and told his disciples to sit there while he went to pray. He wanted time alone with God.
entries.26:37: He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, and he became deeply sad and troubled. Even Jesus felt heavy grief and distress.
entries.26:38: Jesus told them his soul was so sad it felt like dying, and asked them to stay awake and watch with him. He wanted their company and support in his pain.
entries.26:39: He went a little farther, fell on his face, and prayed that if possible this cup of suffering would pass from him, but that God's will, not his own, would be done. He was willing to accept God's plan even though it was painful.
entries.26:40: Jesus came back to the disciples and found them asleep, and he asked Peter if they couldn't stay awake with him for even one hour. He was disappointed that they couldn't support him in his hardest moment.
entries.26:41: Jesus tells his friends to stay awake and pray so they won't give in to temptation. It's a reminder that we may sincerely want to do right, but our weak human nature needs God's help through prayer.
entries.26:42: Jesus prays a second time, asking that if there's no other way, God's will be done. It shows him choosing to trust and obey God even when it's painful, and it invites us to do the same.
entries.26:43: Jesus comes back and finds his disciples asleep because they were exhausted. It shows how alone he was in his hardest moment, since even his closest friends couldn't stay awake with him.
entries.26:44: Jesus leaves them again and prays the same prayer a third time. His repeated prayer shows how deeply he was struggling and how earnestly he was seeking God.
entries.26:45: Jesus wakes the disciples and tells them the time has come for him to be handed over to sinful men. The waiting is over, and what he prayed about is now happening.
entries.26:46: Jesus tells them to get up and go, because the one betraying him is close by. He faces what's coming head-on instead of running away.
entries.26:47: While Jesus is still speaking, Judas arrives with an armed crowd sent by the religious leaders. The betrayal comes from one of his own twelve closest followers.
entries.26:48: Judas had arranged a signal with the crowd: the man he kisses is the one to arrest. He used a sign of friendship to hand Jesus over.
entries.26:49: Judas goes straight to Jesus, calls him Master, and kisses him. The greeting that should mean love and respect was actually the signal for betrayal.
entries.26:50: Jesus calls Judas 'friend' and tells him to do what he came to do, and then they seize him. Jesus doesn't resist or lash out; he accepts what's happening.
entries.26:51: One of Jesus' followers pulls out a sword and cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant. It shows how quickly people turn to violence to defend what they love.
entries.26:52: Jesus tells him to put the sword away, because those who use violence will be destroyed by it. He refuses to fight evil with more evil.
entries.26:53: Jesus points out that he could ask his Father and get a huge army of angels right then. He had the power to escape but chose not to use it.
entries.26:54: Jesus asks how the Scriptures could then come true, since they say this must happen. He was willing to suffer because it was part of God's plan.
entries.26:55: Jesus asks the crowd why they came with weapons to arrest him like a criminal, when he taught openly in the Temple every day. It shows how unfair and underhanded the arrest was.
entries.26:56: Jesus says all this happened to fulfill what the prophets wrote, and then all his disciples ran away. Even his closest followers abandoned him when things got dangerous.
entries.26:57: The men who arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the religious leaders had gathered. His trial before the authorities was beginning.
entries.26:58: Peter followed Jesus from a distance and sat with the servants in the courtyard to see how it would end. He wanted to stay close but was afraid to be seen with Jesus.
entries.26:59: The chief priests and the whole council were trying to find false evidence against Jesus so they could put him to death. They had already decided the outcome and just wanted a reason.
entries.26:60: Even with many false witnesses coming forward, they couldn't find anything that would stick. Their case against Jesus was falling apart because he had done nothing wrong.
entries.26:61: Finally two men claimed Jesus said he could destroy God's Temple and rebuild it in three days. They twisted his words to make them sound like a threat.
entries.26:62: The high priest stands up and asks Jesus if he has any answer to these accusations. Jesus' silence shows his calm and his trust in God.
entries.26:63: Jesus stays silent, so the high priest puts him under oath and demands to know if he is the Christ, the Son of God. This was the key question of the whole trial.
entries.26:64: Jesus answers that it is as he says, and warns that they will see him seated at God's right hand and coming on the clouds. He openly claims to be the Messiah and the judge to come.
entries.26:65: The high priest tears his clothes in outrage and says Jesus has spoken blasphemy, claiming no more witnesses are needed. He treats Jesus' claim as an insult against God.
entries.26:66: The high priest asks the council for their verdict, and they answer that Jesus deserves to die. The religious leaders had condemned him.
entries.26:67: They spit on Jesus, hit him, and mocked him, telling him to prophesy and say who struck him. He was humiliated and abused without fighting back.
entries.26:68: They taunt him to act like a prophet and name who hit him. It shows how cruelly they mocked his claim to speak for God.
entries.26:69: Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard when a servant girl said he had been with Jesus from Galilee. The pressure on Peter was starting.
entries.26:70: Peter denies it in front of everyone, saying he doesn't know what she's talking about. Fear made him lie about his connection to Jesus.
entries.26:71: When Peter moved to the gateway, another girl saw him and told the people there that he had been with Jesus of Nazareth. The accusation followed him.
entries.26:72: Peter denies it again, this time swearing an oath that he doesn't know the man. His denial was getting stronger as his fear grew.
entries.26:73: A little later, people standing nearby tell Peter he really is one of them because his accent gives him away. He couldn't hide who he was.
entries.26:74: Peter starts cursing and swearing that he doesn't know Jesus, and right then a rooster crows. His third denial happened exactly as Jesus had predicted.
entries.26:75: Peter remembers Jesus' words that he would deny him three times before the rooster crowed, and he goes out and weeps bitterly. His failure hit him hard, and he was deeply sorry.
entries.27:1: The religious leaders met early in the morning and decided together that Jesus must die. It shows how far people will go when envy and fear take over their hearts.
entries.27:2: They tied Jesus up and handed him over to Pilate, the Roman governor who had power to sentence him. Jesus was treated like a criminal even though he had done nothing wrong.
entries.27:3: Judas saw that Jesus was really going to be killed, and he was filled with regret, so he brought the thirty silver coins back to the leaders. Guilt caught up with him once he saw the result of what he had done.
entries.27:4: Judas admitted he had done wrong by handing over an innocent man, but the leaders coldly told him that was his problem, not theirs. They cared nothing about the harm they had caused.
entries.27:5: Judas threw the money into the Temple and then killed himself by hanging. His sorrow was real, but it led him to despair instead of to hope.
entries.27:6: The priests picked up the money but said it was not lawful to put it in the Temple treasury because it was blood money. They were careful about a rule while ignoring the far greater wrong they had done.
entries.27:7: They used the money to buy a field where foreigners who died could be buried. Even their attempt to do something proper came out of money paid for a betrayal.
entries.27:8: Because of this, the field became known as the Field of Blood. The place itself kept reminding people of what had happened there.
entries.27:9: This fulfilled what the prophet had spoken about the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on a man by the people of Israel. God's words from long before came true even through a wicked act.
entries.27:10: The money was used to buy the potter's field, exactly as the Lord had directed the prophet to say. It shows that God's plan stands even when people act badly.
entries.27:11: Pilate asked Jesus directly if he was the King of the Jews, and Jesus answered that it was as he said. Jesus did not deny who he was, even before the man with power to kill him.
entries.27:12: When the leaders made their accusations against him, Jesus said nothing at all. He chose not to argue or defend himself.
entries.27:13: Pilate was surprised and asked Jesus if he heard all the charges against him. He expected a man on trial to fight for his life.
entries.27:14: Jesus gave no answer, not even one word, which left the governor amazed. His silence showed quiet strength and trust rather than weakness.
entries.27:15: It was the custom at the feast for the governor to release one prisoner chosen by the crowd. This set the stage for a choice that would reveal what the people really wanted.
entries.27:16: At that time they were holding a well-known prisoner named Barabbas. He was a real criminal, in contrast to Jesus who was innocent.
entries.27:17: When the crowd gathered, Pilate asked them which man they wanted freed, Barabbas or Jesus called the Christ. He gave them a clear choice between two very different men.
entries.27:18: Pilate understood that the leaders had handed Jesus over out of envy, not because he had done wrong. Envy was driving the whole accusation.
entries.27:19: While Pilate sat on the judge's seat, his wife sent word that she had suffered in a dream because of Jesus and warned him to have nothing to do with that innocent man. Even a outsider was troubled by what was happening.
entries.27:20: The chief priests and leaders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and to demand that Jesus be killed. The crowd was turned against an innocent man by those they trusted.
entries.27:21: Pilate asked the crowd which of the two prisoners they wanted him to release, and they answered, Barabbas. They chose a criminal over Jesus.
entries.27:22: Pilate then asked what he should do with Jesus, called the Christ, and they all shouted that he should be crucified. The demand for his death came from the whole crowd.
entries.27:23: Pilate asked what evil Jesus had done, but the crowd only shouted louder for him to be crucified. No one could name a wrong he had done, yet the cry for his death grew.
entries.27:24: Pilate saw he could not stop the uproar, so he washed his hands in front of the people and said he was not responsible for this innocent man's blood. Washing his hands did not remove his share of the blame.
entries.27:25: The whole crowd answered that they accepted the responsibility for his blood, on themselves and their children. They took on themselves the guilt of what was about to happen.
entries.27:26: Pilate released Barabbas, had Jesus whipped, and handed him over to be crucified. The guilty man went free while the innocent man was punished.
entries.27:27: The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the courtyard and gathered the whole unit around him. He was now surrounded by men who were about to mock him.
entries.27:28: They stripped off his clothes and dressed him in a red robe. They were dressing him up as a pretend king to make fun of him.
entries.27:29: They twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, placed a stick in his hand, and knelt before him mocking him as the King of the Jews. They turned a claim about a king into a cruel joke.
entries.27:30: They spat on him and kept hitting him on the head with the stick. He endured open shame and pain without fighting back.
entries.27:31: After they finished mocking him, they took off the robe, put his own clothes back on, and led him away to be crucified. The mockery ended and the execution began.
entries.27:32: As they were leaving, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon and forced him to carry Jesus' cross. An ordinary bystander was pulled into the story and made to help bear the burden.
entries.27:33: They came to a place called Golgotha, which means the Place of a Skull. The name itself hints at death and grimness.
entries.27:34: They offered Jesus wine mixed with a bitter drug, and after tasting it he refused to drink it. He chose to face his suffering with a clear mind rather than be numbed.
entries.27:35: After they nailed him to the cross, the soldiers divided his clothes among themselves by casting lots. Even his few belongings were taken from him.
entries.27:36: The soldiers sat there and kept watch over him. They guarded a dying man as if he were a common criminal.
entries.27:37: They put a sign above his head that read, This is Jesus, the King of the Jews. The charge posted over him was, in truth, who he really was.
entries.27:38: Two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left. He died among criminals, treated as one of them.
entries.27:39: People walking by insulted him, shaking their heads at him. Even strangers joined in mocking a man who was dying.
entries.27:40: They taunted him to save himself and come down from the cross if he was really the Son of God, throwing back his words about the Temple. They challenged him to prove himself, but he stayed on the cross.
entries.27:41: The religious leaders and elders mocked Jesus while he was dying on the cross. It shows how even respected people can join in cruelty when everyone else is doing it.
entries.27:42: They sneered that he saved others but couldn't save himself, and demanded a miracle to prove who he was. They missed that his refusal to come down was exactly how he was saving them.
entries.27:43: They quoted his claim to trust God and be God's Son, daring God to rescue him. Their mockery shows they didn't understand that God's rescue would come through death, not around it.
entries.27:44: Even the criminals crucified beside Jesus insulted him. This shows how completely alone and rejected Jesus was in his final hours.
entries.27:45: From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land. This signals that something deeply serious and sorrowful was happening, not just an ordinary death.
entries.27:46: Jesus cried out to God asking why he had been abandoned, quoting a psalm of deep anguish. It shows that Jesus truly experienced the pain of being cut off, so you can know God understands your darkest moments.
entries.27:47: Some bystanders misheard his cry and thought he was calling for the prophet Elijah. It shows how confused and mistaken people were about what was really happening.
entries.27:48: One person quickly gave Jesus sour wine to drink from a sponge on a stick. This was a small act of relief offered to a dying man.
entries.27:49: The others told him to stop and wait to see if Elijah would come and rescue Jesus. They were watching as spectators rather than helping.
entries.27:50: Jesus cried out loudly one more time and then died. His death was real and deliberate, not a collapse into unconsciousness.
entries.27:51: At the moment of Jesus' death, the temple curtain tore in two from top to bottom and an earthquake shook the ground. The torn curtain means the barrier between people and God was removed.
entries.27:52: Tombs opened and many dead believers were raised to life. This shows that Jesus' death was the turning point that defeats death itself.
entries.27:53: After Jesus rose, these raised people came out of their tombs and appeared to many in Jerusalem. It was a visible sign that Jesus' resurrection brings life to others too.
entries.27:54: The Roman officer and his soldiers saw the earthquake and everything that happened and were terrified, saying Jesus truly was a son of God. Even a pagan outsider recognized what the religious leaders missed.
entries.27:55: Many women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and cared for his needs were watching from a distance. They stayed faithful when most others had fled.
entries.27:56: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee's sons. These women are named as witnesses, showing they were real people who saw what happened.
entries.27:57: In the evening a rich man named Joseph from Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus, arrived. It shows that not all wealthy or influential people rejected Jesus.
entries.27:58: Joseph asked Pilate for Jesus' body, and Pilate ordered it to be handed over. This gave Jesus an honorable burial instead of being left on the cross.
entries.27:59: Joseph took the body and wrapped it in clean linen cloth. It was a careful, respectful act of love for the dead.
entries.27:60: He laid the body in a new tomb cut out of rock that he had prepared for himself, rolled a huge stone across the entrance, and left. The sealed tomb sets up the story of the resurrection.
entries.27:61: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary sat facing the tomb. They stayed near, which is why they would be the first to see what happened next.
entries.27:62: The next day, the Sabbath, the chief priests and Pharisees went together to Pilate. They were still worried about Jesus even after his death.
entries.27:63: They reminded Pilate that Jesus had said he would rise again after three days. They remembered his prediction, even though they didn't believe it.
entries.27:64: They asked for the tomb to be guarded so the disciples couldn't steal the body and claim he rose. Ironically, their security measures helped prove the resurrection was real.
entries.27:65: Pilate told them to use their own guards and make the tomb as secure as they could. He gave them permission to do whatever seemed necessary.
entries.27:66: So they sealed the stone with an official mark and posted guards at the tomb. The best security they could arrange would soon be powerless against what God was about to do.
entries.28:1: Two women who followed Jesus came to the tomb early on the morning after the Sabbath to see where his body had been laid. It shows their devotion and sets the scene for what God was about to do.
entries.28:2: A powerful angel came down from heaven and rolled the stone away from the tomb, then sat on it. The stone was moved not to let Jesus out but to let the witnesses see in.
entries.28:3: The angel looked bright like lightning and his clothes were as white as snow. This shows he came from God's presence and the moment was holy and extraordinary.
entries.28:4: The guards were so terrified of the angel that they shook and fell down like dead men. Even strong men were powerless before God's messenger.
entries.28:5: The angel told the women not to be afraid because he knew they were looking for Jesus, who had been crucified. God sees your seeking and meets you with comfort rather than fear.
entries.28:6: The angel announced that Jesus was not in the tomb because he had risen, just as he had promised, and invited them to see the empty place. The empty tomb is the proof that Jesus' words came true.
entries.28:7: The women were told to hurry and tell the disciples that Jesus was alive and would meet them in Galilee. The good news was meant to be passed on right away, not kept to themselves.
entries.28:8: The women left quickly, feeling both afraid and very happy, to tell the disciples. Real faith often mixes awe and joy, and it moves us to share what we've heard.
entries.28:9: Jesus himself met the women on the way and greeted them, and they held his feet and worshiped him. The risen Jesus is real and personal, worthy of our worship.
entries.28:10: Jesus told the women not to be afraid and to tell his disciples, whom he called his brothers, to meet him in Galilee. He reassures his followers and calls them family.
entries.28:11: Some of the guards went into the city and reported everything that had happened to the chief priests. The evidence of the resurrection reached even those who opposed Jesus.
entries.28:12: The priests and elders met together, decided on a plan, and paid the guards a large amount of money. Instead of accepting the truth, they tried to cover it up.
entries.28:13: The guards were told to say that Jesus' disciples came at night and stole the body while they were asleep. This was a lie made up to explain away the empty tomb.
entries.28:14: The priests promised to smooth things over with the governor if he heard about it, so the guards wouldn't get in trouble. The cover-up was carefully protected by those in power.
entries.28:15: The guards took the money and did as they were told, and this false story spread among the Jewish people for a long time. Lies about Jesus have been told from the start, but they don't change the truth.
entries.28:16: The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go. They obeyed his instructions and met him where he promised to be.
entries.28:17: When the disciples saw Jesus, they worshiped him, though some still had doubts. Even close followers of Jesus can struggle with doubt, and that doesn't disqualify them.
entries.28:18: Jesus told them that all authority in heaven and on earth had been given to him. The risen Jesus has full power and deserves our trust and obedience.
entries.28:19: Jesus sent his followers to make disciples of people from every nation, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. This is the mission of every Christian: to help others follow Jesus.
entries.28:20: Jesus told them to teach people to obey everything he commanded, and promised to be with them always, to the very end. We are never alone in following or sharing Jesus; he stays with us.
